card: A/B start synchronization: adjust startup lengths so A and B enter steady state in a controlled phase relation; measure partner interference.

model.what: Abstract A/B stream model (no opponents/zombies): dwell pushes, rebuild schedule, partner push on anchor = early trigger, partner push on not-yet-executed worker bytes during rebuild = kill. All 25 (qA,qB) band combos, 200k rounds.
model.results: rev0: A killed by B in 11/25 combos, B never killed by A (A's 400h trail touches only its own lattice point; B's 800h trail covers 2 lattice points, i.e. sweeps A's anchor+worker mid-trail). Startup delays of A or B (2..256 turns) only move the kill times (8-14/25 kills): phase relation drifts ~20 turns per B generation (A gen 275 turns, B gen 531), so startup sync cannot control it. B trail 400h (DX 2800h): 0/25 kills.

candidates.label: C1
candidates.change: B phoenix DX 2400h -> 2800h (B and captured zombies: trail 800h -> 400h, step 2C00h kept)

candidates.label: C2
candidates.change: B main stream DX 2800h (trail 400h), captured zombies keep DX 2400h; DX passed via BP (mov bp,2800h before jmp phoenix_init; mov bp,2400h on zombie path; phoenix_init mov dx,bp)
candidates.notes: Screen ALL +0.012 but multi group clearly negative (-0.104 [-0.173,-0.034], smulti-V6x3 -0.068, smulti-mix -0.139) and lead_V6 -0.194 in screen; dedicated threat job confirms -0.10 [-0.151,-0.049] vs V6-family leads (24 cohorts x 20). Not promising.

threatFindings.threat: Partner crossfire: B's 800h trail sweeps A's anchor/worker mid-trail and kills A when A is rebuilding
threatFindings.evidence: Base trace (job 20261003183133222-A005-trace-nd583, duplicate of B051 trace): 4/161 deaths partner-attributed, all A (CAND1) killed by B (CAND2). Raw jsonl: sthreat-movsw_CodeKiller r65875 and sthreat-movsw_TrojanByte r984 = B trail bytes written over A's worker during rebuild (exact mechanism); CodeKiller r4980 = A already on misaligned anchor (arena =3 mod 4), B's trail FB 0F then fatal; s2025-1 r2071 = misattributed (YANDE wrote the fatal EE FF; the CAND2 bytes were B's identical template at a shared anchor). Abstract model reproduces the asymmetry (A killed 11/25, B 0/25).
threatFindings.impact: ~2 real partner kills per 160 trace battles (~1-2% of deaths); upper bound of gain from removing it ~0.004/battle

threatFindings.threat: Startup timing (phase relation of A and B steady states) controls partner interference
threatFindings.evidence: Model: delays 2..256 turns on A or B leave kills at 8-14/25 combos, only shifting kill rounds; A004's one-turn phase probes (screens yx4ug +0.0012, ujom1 -0.0021) are at noise.
threatFindings.impact: none; do not spend effort on startup-phase sync

threatFindings.threat: Shortening B's trail to 400h (partner-safe) loses badly vs V6-family opponents
threatFindings.evidence: C2 threat job 20261003185939605-A005-threat-6igxq: -0.100 [-0.151,-0.049], lead_V6 -0.072, lead_V4 -0.093, lead_V6Guard -0.135; threat team scores rise to 0.53 from 0.45-0.49. Screens: lead_V6 -0.172 (C1) and -0.194 (C2).
threatFindings.impact: Mechanism hypothesis: the same mid-trail sweep that kills our A is B's weapon against same-lattice (52h, 0FFBh) opponents' A streams; with 400h B only touches shared points. Also doubles B rebuild exposure.

threatFindings.threat: Captured zombies on 400h trails cost ~0.02 (C1 vs C2 differ only in zombie DX)
threatFindings.evidence: C1 ALL -0.009 vs C2 ALL +0.012 (2025: -0.020 vs +0.014); difference is within the chaotic-screen noise band; untested directly.

recommendation: Do not promote C1 or C2. Partner interference is real but small (A killed by B's 800h trail ~1-2% of deaths) and cannot be controlled by startup phase (drift randomizes it). The structural fix (B trail 400h) removes B's offensive mid-trail sweep and loses ~0.10 vs V6-family leads. Keep B at DX 2400h. Partner-safe alternatives would need lockstep motion (A014) or a common 800h sublattice for both streams, with expected gain <= ~0.004.
